title: An Adaptive SMOTE Oversampling Algorithm Based on Dynamic Data Schema Adjustment
abstract: Class imbalance remains a critical challenge in the fields of machine learning and data mining, where standard classifiers often exhibit a strong bias toward the majority class. Although the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) is widely used to mitigate this issue, its blind linear interpolation strategy often introduces noise and causes severe class overlapping, especially near the decision boundaries. To address these limitations, this paper proposes an Adaptive Schema SMOTE (AS-SMOTE) algorithm based on dynamic data schema adjustment. The core idea of AS-SMOTE is to dynamically analyze the local density and spatial characteristics of minority class samples prior to generating new instances. By computing a boundary awareness factor and assessing feature variances within the local neighborhood, the algorithm adaptively constructs a feature schema weight for each dimension. This schema weight is then integrated into a dynamic regulation vector that constrains the interpolation process. When generating new samples, the algorithm automatically balances generalization capability and pattern adherence: it allows standard random interpolation in safe minority regions, while strictly confining the synthetic instances along the tightly distributed feature "schemas" near the decision boundaries. Theoretical framework analysis demonstrates that AS-SMOTE effectively prevents synthetic samples from invading the majority class space, preserves the local topological structure of the minority class, and enhances the classification performance and robustness of downstream models on imbalanced datasets.

title: A Semantic Constraint SMOTE Over-sampling Method for Imbalanced Data
abstract: Class imbalance is a pervasive challenge in machine learning and data mining, widely observed in real-world scenarios such as credit fraud detection, medical diagnosis, and network intrusion detection. The scarcity of minority class samples often forces traditional classification models to severely bias toward the majority class during training, thereby drastically reducing the recognition accuracy of critical minority cases. As one of the most classic over-sampling techniques, the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) alleviates structural imbalance by performing linear interpolation between neighboring minority samples. However, traditional SMOTE relies solely on geometric distance in the feature space, completely ignoring the inherent business logic and semantic constraints of the underlying data. Consequently, the synthesized virtual samples often violate real-world rule logic consistency, introducing a multitude of invalid "phantom samples" or heavy noise. To address this critical flaw, this paper proposes an improved SMOTE algorithm incorporating semantic constraints, termed SC-SMOTE (Semantic Constraint SMOTE). This approach translates domain expert knowledge and logical rules into mathematical semantic constraint functions, embedding a new neighbor filtering mechanism and a boundary projection correction strategy into the traditional interpolation process. This paper comprehensively details the theoretical foundation, mathematical modeling, and algorithmic workflow of SC-SMOTE. The proposed algorithm not only expands the minority class within the geometric space but also rigorously guarantees the validity and rationality of the generated data within the semantic space. This research offers a novel paradigm for empowering data-driven machine learning models with expert-guided knowledge.

title: Attention-route SMOTE: Oversampling via Attention Flow Guided Generation Paths
abstract: Class imbalance is a pervasive challenge in machine learning, where standard classifiers often exhibit a bias towards the majority class. Although the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) is widely used to mitigate this issue, its reliance on local Euclidean distances and random linear interpolation frequently leads to over-sampling in noisy or overlapping regions, while failing to preserve the global topological structure of the data. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a novel oversampling algorithm named Attention-route SMOTE. Instead of blindly interpolating between geometric neighbors, the proposed method leverages the self-attention mechanism to explicitly model the global feature correlations among minority class samples, thereby constructing an "attention flow matrix." During the synthesis process, new samples are generated along optimized attention paths, further corrected by an attention context vector that integrates global manifold trends. This attention-guided routing ensures that the synthesized samples not only inherit local characteristics but also conform to the underlying global data distribution. Consequently, Attention-route SMOTE effectively expands the minority class space, enhances sample diversity, and maintains distinct class boundaries without introducing structural noise.

title: A Novel Enterprise AI Classification Framework for Business Transformation: A Structured Literature Review and Integration of AI Types and Autonomy Levels
abstract: Enterprise investment in artificial intelligence has reached an unprecedented scale across national, regional, and organisational levels of the economy, yet transformation outcomes remain highly variable. Recent global research indicates that the majority of enterprise AI investments produce no measurable profit-and-loss impact, with only a minority of organisations extracting material enterprise-level value. Without an integrated classification framework that allows enterprises to deploy, govern, and create value from the full range of AI technologies and autonomy levels across enterprise functions, the risks of misallocated investment, fragmented deployment, and unrealised return remain difficult to mitigate. A structured literature review on AI classification reveals that existing frameworks do not integrate AI technology types, operational autonomy levels, and concrete enterprise applications in a single classification structure that can support enterprise AI-driven transformation decisions. To address this gap, this paper proposes the Enterprise AI Classification Framework, a novel classification model that integrates six AI technology types with six autonomy levels in a 6 × 6 matrix of 36 combinations, each corresponding to concrete business applications across enterprise functions. A computational pilot study (n = 20 cases for case-based coding validation and 12 LLM-simulated personas × 30 vignettes for role-specific hypothesis pre-specification) provides preliminary evidence of substantially higher classification coverage than four baseline frameworks and pre-specifies role-divergence hypotheses for a planned empirical validation, with all design choices locked in an OSF pre-registration; reliability point estimates exceed the pre-specified α≥0.70 threshold at the pilot scale, with bootstrapped confidence intervals expected to tighten under the full-corpus run in the follow-up study. An interview-based empirical validation with approximately 250 decision-makers and practitioners across 20 industries is in preparation.

title: Named entity recognition in water conservancy field based on multi-feature fusion and boundary perception
abstract: Named entity recognition in the water conservancy field is a crucial step in extracting water conservancy information, playing a key role in constructing water conservancy knowledge graphs and enhancing water conservancy knowledge question answering systems. However, existing methods still face challenges when dealing with text data in the field, including semantic diversity of entities, ambiguity in entity boundaries and insufficient feature utilization, resulting in limited recognition performance. To address these issues, this paper proposes a Named Entity Recognition Model based on Multi-feature Fusion and Boundary Perception (MFBP-NER). The model extracts multi-source features from three dimensions namely characters, pinyin, and dictionaries to obtain a more semantically rich feature representation. On this basis, an Adaptive Gating Fusion (AGF) mechanism is proposed to achieve dynamic weighting and effective fusion among multiple features, fully exploiting the deep semantic interaction relationships across different feature dimensions. Meanwhile, a BiGRU network is employed to further capture context dependencies and long-distance relationships within sequences. Additionally, a boundary perception module is incorporated into the global pointer framework to model semantic dependency relationships between spans, thereby enhancing entity boundary differences and enabling more accurately determine entity boundary. To evaluate the performance of MFBP-NER, experiments are conducted on three datasets with varying granularity. The results show that the proposed model achieves higher F1 scores compared to baseline models, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed approach in named entity recognition within the water conservancy field. It provides a viable technical foundation for constructing water conservancy knowledge graphs and developing question answering systems.

title: AgentLTL: A Trace-Verification Framework for Measuring, Enforcing, and Training Procedural Compliance in Tool-Using LLM Agents
abstract: Tool-using LLM agents are usually evaluated by final-answer correctness or LLM judges. Neither captures how an answer was produced. In safety-critical settings, the procedure itself is part of correctness. In this paper, we introduce AgentLTL, a language derived from First-Order Linear Temporal Logic (FO-LTL) that expresses procedural rules over agent traces. It yields a deterministic, judge-free compliance score. In this framework, a single specification drives two usages. The first is harnessing: the constraints score completed traces, or gate tool calls by checking each prefix online, before execution. The second is finetuning: the score serves as a dense reward. On a benchmark spanning ordering, branching, iteration, and grounding, block-and-warn harnessing improves compliance on five of seven models. Finetuning with the same reward yields +38 and +17.5 percentage point gains in accuracy and compliance on held-out patterns, including unseen tool-name aliases. These findings are consistent with the model acquiring procedural structure rather than memorizing surface tool names and procedures.

title: Topological Neural Dynamics: A Neuron-wise Framework for Sequence Modeling
abstract: Existing sequence models, including RNNs, LSTMs, continuous-time networks, and Transformers, share a common structural principle: layer-wise dynamics, where all neurons in the same layer co-evolve through a shared parameterized operator, leaving individual neurons no freedom to evolve independently. Yet in many complex dynamical systems, rich global behavior emerges precisely from locally evolving units interacting through structured connectivity. Inspired by this principle, we introduce Topological Neural Dynamics (TND), a sequence modeling framework that shifts computation from layer-wise to neuron-wise dynamics. TND represents a neural system as a directed neuron graph, an interaction operator, and a local dynamics function, where each neuron evolves independently and collective computation emerges from interactions through the explicit graph topology. We instantiate TND as a discrete-time graph-coupled dynamical system and evaluate it as a case study on a behavior cloning task in single-player Pong. Compared with Vanilla RNN, Sparse RNN, LSTM, Closed-form continuous-time neural network (CfC), and Transformer baselines, TND achieves the best catch rate and a mean of 17.47 consecutive catches per round, more than three times that of the strongest baseline. These results suggest that shifting from layer-wise to neuron-wise dynamics provides an effective inductive bias for sequence modeling.

title: Information Leakage Envelopes
abstract: We study privacy guarantees in the framework of pointwise maximal leakage (PML) that satisfy two requirements: they are robust under post-processing and upper bound the failure probability, i.e., the probability that the information leakage exceeds a given threshold. We first examine two candidate definitions inspired by (approximate) differential privacy and show that neither one satisfies both requirements simultaneously. We then introduce the notion of the PML envelope, which quantifies the largest amount of information leakage about a secret after arbitrary post-processing of a mechanism's output. By construction, the PML envelope satisfies both requirements. We discuss basic structural properties of the envelope, such as monotonicity, and derive general upper and lower bounds. We further analyze the envelope for two widely used privacy mechanisms: the PML-extremal mechanisms in the high-privacy regime and randomized response. Overall, this work establishes the PML envelope as a natural and operationally meaningful definition for providing privacy guarantees that are preserved under arbitrary downstream transformations.

title: Counterfactual-Consistency SMOTE: Causal-Consistent Minority Oversampling via Structural Causal Models
abstract: Class imbalance is a pervasive challenge in machine learning, often leading to biased classifiers that perform poorly on minority classes. Although the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) and its variants are widely used to mitigate this issue by interpolating new samples in the feature space, they fundamentally ignore the underlying causal relationships among variables. Consequently, these methods frequently generate logically impossible or physically counter-intuitive samples that violate real-world constraints, introducing harmful noise into the training process. To address this limitation, this paper proposes Counterfactual-consistency SMOTE (CC-SMOTE), a novel data augmentation framework that integrates structural causal models (SCMs) and counterfactual inference into the oversampling process. Instead of performing naive algebraic interpolation in the endogenous observation space, CC-SMOTE first learns the causal graph from data and estimates the underlying structural equations. It then abducts the observed minority samples into the mutually independent exogenous noise space, conducts linear interpolation within this latent space, and reconstructs the endogenous features via counterfactual downstream propagation under specified causal constraints. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that while traditional SMOTE inherently suffers from causal violation bias when dealing with non-linear mechanisms, CC-SMOTE strictly guarantees the causal fidelity and structural consistency of all synthesized samples. This approach offers a theoretically grounded and reliable solution for class-imbalanced learning in safety-critical and high-stakes domains.

title: ГЕНЕРАЦІЯ SQL-ЗАПИТІВ З ТЕКСТУ ЗА ДОПОМОГОЮ ВЕЛИКИХ МОВНИХ МОДЕЛЕЙ
abstract: ГЕНЕРАЦІЯ SQL-ЗАПИТІВ З ТЕКСТУ ЗА ДОПОМОГОЮ ВЕЛИКИХ МОВНИХ МОДЕЛЕЙ Анотація.Розглянуто проблему генерації SQL-запитів до баз даних за допомогою великих мовних моделей на основі текстових запитів користувача.Основну увагу було приділено дослідженню та розробці Text-to-SQL пайплайну для автоматизованої генерації SQL-запитів на основі запитів природною мовою.При цьому необхідно було зменшити затримку генерації SQL-запитів і підвищити їхню коректність у середовищі великомасштабної реляційної бази даних.Для досягнення цієї мети було запропоновано використання динамічного скорочення схеми, за якого до великої мовної моделі передається не повна схема бази даних, а лише релевантні фрагменти схеми для конкретного запиту користувача.На підставі проведених досліджень було спроектовано та програмно реалізовано Text-to-SQL пайплайн із динамічним скороченням схеми бази даних.Система, зокрема, містить витяг SQL-визначень таблиць, побудову індексу схеми, вибір релевантних таблиць, формування скороченого контексту схеми, побудову промпту, генерацію SQLзапиту та його валідацію перед виконанням.Для тестування та перевірки коректності згенерованих SQL-запитів використовувалися PostgreSQL і pgAdmin.Був проведений чисельний експерімент.Використовувався набір з понад 200 тестових запитань, згрупованих у 9 категорій.У результаті оптимізований пайплайн зменшив середній час генерації SQL-запиту на 86,75%.Водночас, частка успішно згенерованих SQL-запитів зросла з 51,77% до 69,85%.Отримані результати підтверджують ефективність динамічного скорочення схеми для покращення швидкодії та коректності Text-to-SQL № 5(59) 2026

title: English-Normalized Text and Topic Analytics for FixMyStreet Brussels: Spatio-Temporal Hotspot Detection and Decision Support from Citizen Reports
abstract: Citizen-reporting platforms generate high-volume, multilingual streams of service requests, yet operational triage often relies on coarse category labels and manual inspection. This study develops an explainable analytics pipeline with probability calibration for FixMyStreet Brussels reports, combining text-based urgency modeling, topic discovery, and spatio-temporal hotspot scoring to inform municipal analytic review. From 522,132 raw reports, we build an English-normalized text field for modeling, derive resolution-time outcomes from closed cases, and curate a 1000-item gold standard with an explicit high-urgency class. A TF-IDF logistic regression baseline achieves reasonable classification performance on the labeled split and, after probability calibration, yields confidence estimates that are more suitable for risk-aware prioritization than uncalibrated scores. Topic-level analyses reveal dominant themes related to sidewalks, road damage, and bulky waste, and hotspot scores highlight persistent, high-impact issue clusters. Event detection on aggregated signals did not identify events above the predefined z-score threshold during the analysis window, suggesting that the observed dynamics are more visible as chronic, recurring problems than as abrupt threshold-level anomalies. title: Theoretical Modeling of Ising Spin Communication Channels with Relaxed-State Modulation
abstract: This capsule provides the Python/MATLAB reproducibility package for the article “Theoretical Modeling of Ising Spin Communication Channels with Relaxed-State Modulation.” The capsule demonstrates the relaxed-state Ising communication model in three complementary ways. First, it runs a small live 2D toy example in which random Ising media are generated, a classical bit is written by local perturbations of couplings and fields near the transmit sites, the medium is relaxed to its ground state, and the bit is decoded by Bob using a private differential readout and by Charlie using only public features. Second, it regenerates the published figures and tables from stored per-figure data using MATLAB plotters for Figs. 5–10 and Python plotters for Tables 7–8. Third, it runs each production data-generation pipeline at reduced scale to verify that the full simulation workflow executes end-to-end inside Code Ocean. The default `run.sh` script executes the live toy, regenerates all stored-data figures/tables, and then runs the reduced-scale full pipeline. Generated figure/table images are copied to `/results`, and reduced-scale reports and CSV/config outputs are copied to `/results/outputs`. The stored `figs/*/data/` files correspond to the published-scale figure data, while the `figs/*/data_gen/` folders contain the production data-generation scripts and readme files documenting the larger HPC commands. The reduced-scale Code Ocean run is intended to verify reproducibility of the code paths and plotting pipeline within a reasonable runtime; it does not rerun the full cluster-scale campaigns.

title: Evaluating Agentic Harness Systems for Autonomous Computational Pathology
abstract: Autonomous computational pathology (ACP) converts high-level pathology analysis goals into executable, traceable and clinically bounded workflows. Realizing this capability requires adapting general agentic harness systems to pathology-specific tasks, tools, evidence standards and clinical claim boundaries. We contribute ACP-Bench, a framework that adapts existing harness systems from computational pathology support toward ACP workflow capability. ACP-Bench evaluates 41 pathology workflow tasks, including 24 biomarker, 7 morphology and 10 prognosis tasks spanning 6 body-system groups and 9 endpoint families. The benchmark evaluates 9 models and 3 harness groups (Claude Code, Codex and Open Code), yielding 369 complete trajectories. ACP-Bench evaluates each trajectory across workflow execution, diagnostic performance and clinical-boundary alignment, combining expert-adjudicated process audits, diagnostic assessment and pathologist-validated safety review. Across evaluated systems, workflow initiation, task interpretation and diagnostic reporting were more mature than tool-bound execution, result binding and reflective workflow revision, and formal end-to-end completion remained rare. ACP-Bench provides a reusable standard for auditing whether agentic systems can operationalize pathology workflows before claims of reliable clinical autonomy.

title: Benchmarking LLM Agents on Meta-Analysis Articles from Nature Portfolio
abstract: Meta-analysis is a demanding form of evidence synthesis that combines literature retrieval, PI/ECO-guided study selection, and statistical aggregation. Its structured, verifiable workflow makes it an ideal substrate for evaluating systematic scientific reasoning, yet existing benchmarks lack ground truth across the full retrieval-screening-synthesis pipeline. We introduce MetaSyn, a dataset of 442 expert-curated meta-analyses from Nature Portfolio journals. Each entry pairs a research question with PI/ECO criteria, a retrieval corpus of 140k PubMed articles, verified positive studies, hard negatives that are topically similar but PI/ECO-ineligible, and complete search strategies and date bounds. Benchmarking twelve pipeline configurations (nine RAG variants and a protocol-driven agent) reveals a critical screening bottleneck: despite a retrieval ceiling of 90.9% recall at K=200, no system recovers more than 52.7% of ground-truth included literature. Current LLMs fail to reliably separate eligible studies from PI/ECO-failing distractors in pools of comparable topical relevance. Stage-attributed metrics capture where systems succeed and fail; a single end-to-end score does not.

title: Software Between Quantum and Machine Learning - and Down to Pulses
abstract: Contemporary quantum computing platforms remain, in essence, programmable physical systems whose control is typically mediated through unitary gate abstractions. While such abstractions provide a uniform interface, they obscure important aspects of the underlying hardware and may limit the exploitation of its full capabilities. Direct operation at the control-pulse level offers a more expressive and physically faithful paradigm, enabling, for instance, the implementation of tailored error-mitigation and optimisation strategies. However, this increased expressivity comes at the cost of greater quantum software development complexity, necessitating structured and accessible tooling. We present a software framework, integrated within the QML-Essentials package, that extends quantum machine learning (QML) methodologies to encompass pulse-level modelling. By embedding quantum optimal control techniques within a QML setting, our approach enables the seamless combination of gate-based and pulse-level representations. The framework provides a comprehensive suite of modelling and analytical capabilities. In particular, we introduce composable ansatz constructions based on interchangeable building blocks, and support for end-to-end optimisation of pulse parameters. Motivated by the central role of quantum Fourier models, we further incorporate a range of Fourier-analytic diagnostics, complemented by extended measures of entanglement. All performance-critical components are implemented in a high-performance environment using JAX and supported by a dedicated quantum simulator. Taken together, the framework facilitates reproducible and systematic investigations, while bridging the conceptual and practical divide between abstract circuit models and hardware-aware optimisation. It provides a robust foundation for future developments at the intersection of QML and quantum control.

title: Consumer Perception and Preferences towards AI Chatbots: An Empirical Study of E-Commerce Users in Ludhiana
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) chatbots have become a defining feature of the online shopping experience, reshaping the way e-commerce platforms communicate with and serve their customers. This study examines consumer perception, trust, and attitude toward AI chatbots in the context of online retail, and identifies the key factors that drive their preference and adoption among shoppers. An analytical research design was adopted, with primary data gathered through a structured questionnaire administered to 145 respondents from Ludhiana who had prior experience using AI chatbots while shopping online. Respondents were selected through random sampling, and the resulting data were examined using mean analysis and exploratory factor analysis. The findings indicate that consumers hold a broadly favourable view of AI chatbots, rating them positively for their helpfulness, ease of use, and convenience during the purchase process. Attitudes toward chatbot usage were equally encouraging, pointing to a growing willingness among consumers to rely on AI-driven assistance while shopping online. Trust, while moderately high overall, was tempered by lingering concerns over data privacy, security, and the reliability of chatbot responses. Exploratory factor analysis further revealed three underlying dimensions shaping chatbot adoption: User Acceptance, Perceived Convenience, and Behavioural Intention. Taken together, the results suggest that while AI chatbots are increasingly seen as valuable shopping companions, e-commerce businesses must continue to invest in stronger data security, deeper personalization, and more responsive design if they are to fully earn consumer trust and sustain long-term adoption. Keywords: Consumer Perception, Trust, Attitude, AI Chatbots, Consumer Preferences, Customer Satisfaction, E-commerce

title: Scaling Model Size and Zero-Shot Cross-Lingual Transfer Performance in English Intermediate-Task Training
abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. We investigate whether English intermediate-task training is still helpful on non-English target tasks. Using nine intermediate language-understanding tasks, we evaluate intermediate-task transfer in a zero-shot cross-lingual setting on the XTREME benchmark. We see large improvements from intermediate training on the BUCC and Tatoeba sentence retrieval tas Research goal: How does the scaling of model size affect the zero-shot cross-lingual transfer performance of English intermediate-task training, as measured by F1 scores on the XTREME benchmark? title: Data-Consistency Loop SMOTE: A Closed-Loop Over-sampling Algorithm for High-Dimensional Imbalanced Data
abstract: Class imbalance is a pervasive challenge in machine learning, often leading to biased classifiers that perform poorly on the minority class. Although the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) is widely used to mitigate this issue, its blind linear interpolation mechanism frequently introduces noisy samples and causes boundary blurring, failing to preserve the underlying distribution of the original data. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a novel over-sampling framework named Data-Consistency Loop SMOTE (DCL-SMOTE). Unlike traditional unidirectional sampling approaches, DCL-SMOTE establishes a self-adaptive, closed-loop iteration system driven by a "generation -> consistency check -> correction -> re-generation" workflow. The proposed algorithm evaluates each synthetic candidate through multi-dimensional consistency checkers encompassing probability distribution, spatial geometry, and manifold structure. Samples failing the evaluation are dynamically adjusted via gradient-based optimization in the correction module or discarded to trigger a feedback mechanism that adaptively refines the sampling weights of the baseline minority instances. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that the closed-loop feedback and self-healing mechanism effectively ensure that the generated samples conform strictly to the authentic minority distribution. This framework provides a robust and mathematically rigorous solution for pattern recognition and classification tasks in high-dimensional imbalanced domains.

title: An Improved SMOTE Oversampling Algorithm Based on a Multi-Strategy Voting Mechanism
abstract: Classifying imbalanced data remains a critical challenge in machine learning, as standard algorithms often favor the majority class and compromise the classification accuracy of the minority class. The Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) alleviates this issue by interpolating new samples linearly. However, its uniform generation strategy frequently introduces noisy data and blurs class boundaries. To address these limitations, this paper proposes an improved SMOTE algorithm based on a multi-strategy voting mechanism, termed Data-voting SMOTE. Unlike traditional approaches that rely on a single geometric model, the proposed method concurrently deploys three distinct generation strategies: standard linear interpolation, Gaussian perturbation center expansion, and three-point recombination centroiding. To ensure the quality of the synthesized data, a multi-indicator evaluation framework is established to quantify the spatial properties of each candidate sample based on density security and distance harmony. A majority voting mechanism then filters these candidates, accepting the final synthetic sample only when a consensus is reached among the strategies. This collaborative approach significantly enhances sample diversity while preserving sharp decision boundaries, thereby effectively reducing noise generation and improving the generalization performance of classifiers on imbalanced datasets.

title: A Contrastive Boundary Push SMOTE Over-sampling Algorithm for Imbalanced Data Learning
abstract: Class imbalance is a pervasive challenge in machine learning, where classifiers often bias toward the majority class due to the skewed distribution of data. The Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) alleviates this by interpolating synthetic instances within the minority class space. However, traditional SMOTE frequently generates samples that invade the majority class region, leading to severe class-overlapping and blurred decision boundaries. To address this limitation, this paper proposes a novel over-sampling method named Contrastive Boundary Push SMOTE (CBP-SMOTE). The core idea of CBP-SMOTE is to explicitly integrate the philosophy of contrastive learning into the data generation process. Specifically, after synthesizing a baseline instance, the algorithm identifies its nearest neighbor in the majority (negative) class space and constructs a push vector. By leveraging a distance-based feedback mechanism, the baseline instance is explicitly pushed away from the negative class representation space. This mechanism effectively sharpens the decision boundary and suppresses the overlapping effect. Theoretical and procedural analyses demonstrate that the proposed algorithm significantly clarifies class boundaries while maintaining the diversity of the minority class, thereby enhancing the generalization performance of classifiers on imbalanced datasets.

title: Multi-View SMOTE: Separate Generation and Alignment for High-Dimensional Imbalanced Multi-View Learning
abstract: Multi-view learning has emerged as a powerful paradigm in machine learning, where objects are characterized by multiple heterogeneous feature subsets or data sources. However, the ubiquitous class imbalance problem significantly undermines the classification performance in real-world multi-view applications. Traditional synthetic minority over-sampling techniques (SMOTE) are primarily designed for single-view data and fail to handle the complex structural correlations across different views. Directly applying single-view SMOTE to each view independently disrupts the alignment and cross-view consistency of the synthesized data, while feature concatenation severely exacerbates the curse of dimensionality. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a novel over-sampling framework named Multi-view SMOTE. The proposed algorithm decomposes the multi-view over-sampling process into a separate generation stage and a joint alignment stage. In the first stage, raw synthetic minority samples are independently generated within each distinct feature space using localized topological interpolation, preserving the specific characteristics of each individual view. In the second stage, a multi-view alignment mechanism is established by mapping all views into a unified lower-dimensional latent subspace. Cross-view consistency is enforced by minimizing the discrepancy among the projected representations of the minority class. A consensus representation is subsequently synthesized in the latent space and back-projected to the original view-specific spaces via pseudo-inverse reconstruction, ensuring that the final synthetic samples are perfectly aligned across all views. Theoretical formulations validate that Multi-view SMOTE effectively prevents semantic misalignment while mitigating the curse of dimensionality. The proposed framework provides an efficient, robust, and highly interpretable data-augmentation solution for imbalanced multi-view classification tasks.

title: Physics-Informed Imitation Learning for Resilient Autonomous Driving
abstract: Imitation learning has emerged as a promising paradigm for autonomous vehicle control. However, existing policies often suffer from severe covariate shift and lack explicit stability guarantees in closed-loop trajectory tracking. This paper proposes an adaptive Lyapunov-constrained imitation learning framework for vehicle trajectory tracking. To address the covariate shift problem, we explicitly embed a discrete-time kinematic bicycle model into the policy training process. This differentiable physical prior enables propagation of the nominal tracking error and allows a global Lyapunov decay constraint to be directly employed on the policy optimization via an Actor-Critic architecture. To prevent the overly aggressive penalization near the reference trajectory, we introduce a state-dependent adaptive decay rate that relaxes the constraint for small errors while strengthening it under large deviations. As a result, the proposed method achieves both high tracking precision and strong recovery from model uncertainties and disturbances. Extensive experiments in interactive traffic environments demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in collision avoidance and disturbance rejection.

title: OmniPresent: Generating Coherent Presentation Suites from Scientific Papers
abstract: Transforming static research papers into dynamic media such as posters, slides, and videos is essential for effective dissemination but remains a labor-intensive challenge. Existing automated approaches often treat these formats in isolation and consequently fail to maintain semantic consistency across the entire presentation suite. We address this fragmentation by formalizing the task of unified presentation suite generation and proposing OmniPresent to orchestrate the creation of coherent deliverables. Our framework adopts a renderable HTML representation to enable centralized content planning and a self-correcting verify-and-repair loop that actively resolves conflicts across modalities. We further facilitate scalable research in this domain by releasing OmniPreBench, a comprehensive dataset comprising over one thousand papers with paired artifacts, and establishing a rigorous VLM-based evaluation protocol. Empirical results confirm that our method generates high-quality and faithful presentation suites that significantly surpass strong baselines in both accuracy and visual appeal.

title: TerraBench: Can Agents Reason Over Heterogeneous Earth-System Data?
abstract: Climate and environmental decision-making increasingly requires reasoning across heterogeneous inputs, including gridded physical data, satellite imagery, geospatial context, and simulator outputs. Weather and climate foundation models can forecast well, but do not reason interactively in language, while large language models (LLMs) reason in language but cannot operate directly on high-dimensional Earth-system data. As a result, real scientific workflows in Earth-science remain underserved. We introduce TerraBench, a benchmark for grounded Earth-science reasoning, built on TerraAgent, a ReAct-style executable framework that interleaves reasoning, tool calls, and observations to couple LLM planning with scientific tools for environmental retrieval, geospatial processing, simulation, and artifact-backed computation. TerraBench unifies analysis of Earth observation imagery, gridded data, GIS reasoning and simulation in a single executable interface, whereas prior benchmarks isolate these capabilities into narrow individual tasks. It is also the first in this space to pair process-level tool-use metrics with tolerance-aware numeric scoring. The benchmark comprises 403 extensive agentic tasks across three tracks (Fundamentals, Simulator-Grounded, and Document-Grounded Verification) and eight application domains with 24,500 verified execution steps. These results indicate that reliable Earth-science agents must go beyond tool access to coordinate heterogeneous workflows, parameterize tools precisely, and preserve artifact provenance.

title: BRAÇO PESCADOR ROBÓTICO COMO ESTRATÉGIA PEDAGÓGICA PARA TRABALHAR MOTRICIDADE E ROBÓTICA COM CRIANÇAS
abstract: O ensino precisa evoluir de uma prática em que os alunos são agentes passivos, para outra que os tornem participantes ativos na construção do seu conhecimento. As práticas lúdicas, por serem mais atrativas, facilitam o aprendizado. Assim, a robótica educacional, no desenvolvimento de projetos com aplicação pedagógica, promove o aprendizado de conteúdos de diversas áreas, de forma lúdica, através da experimentação. Esta pesquisa teve como objetivo o desenvolvimento de um Braço Pescador Robótico que utiliza componentes tecnológicos relacionadas à robótica educacional para promover um maior engajamento dos estudantes, desenvolvendo especificamente a motricidade fina de mãos e dedos. Neste sentido, está sendo utilizado em duas escolas da rede municipal de Santa Maria-RS. As escolas de ensino fundamental foram escolhidas para utilizá-lo em diferentes aplicações, com base no currículo e planejamento das professoras. Em uma escola, turma de 1º ano, em outra, pré-escola, 1º e 2º anos. No desenvolvimento das experiências com os alunos, criaram-se novas possibilidades de utilização do Braço Pescador Robótico, no aprendizado de diferentes conteúdos.

title: Finite Consequence Formation: A Release-Validity Criterion for Finite Intelligence
abstract: This record fixes the public release of an 8-page preprint on Finite Consequence Formation. The paper states a release-validity criterion for finite intelligence: before a finite system releases a prediction, proof, diagnosis, scientific claim, control decision, or action as warranted, its finite contact with reality must be structurally sufficient to carry the declared consequence. For a reality space R, a finite contact map C:R->X, and a declared consequence Q:R->Y, the exact release-validity gate is K_C subset K_Q. Equivalently, Q factors through contact, Q=Qbar after C. When the gate fails, a contact cell carries non-flat consequence load, Lambda_{C,Q}(x)=Q(C^{-1}(x)), and forced answering is not a valid substitute for the missing required distinction. The record also includes the static hidden-twin load-repair flagship: the original C+-contact graph has 85/1099 obstructions and the full same-cell graph has 110/1437 obstructions; a deterministic lawful splitter using only frozen C+ contact coordinates reduces both obstruction counts to zero. Six forced-answer systems fail, and 512 random nuisance binary splits never clear all obstructions. This is a static release/repair result, not a dynamic action-CREATE claim.

title: An Improved SMOTE Algorithm Based on Label-Smoothing Generation
abstract: Imbalanced data classification is a challenging problem in the fields of machine learning and data mining. The Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) is a widely used over-sampling method that addresses this issue by linearly interpolating between minority class samples. However, traditional SMOTE assigns absolute hard labels to all synthetic samples, neglecting the ambiguity and uncertainty inherent in boundary regions, which often leads to overfitting and high sensitivity to noise. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes an improved SMOTE algorithm based on label-smoothing generation, termed LSG-SMOTE. Instead of assigning a rigid binary label to newly generated samples, the proposed algorithm analyzes the local neighborhood structure of the seed samples in the feature space and dynamically generates a continuous label distribution (soft labels) for each synthetic sample. This soft label reflects the blending degree of minority and majority classes in that local region, introducing a regularization effect during the training process. A soft-label cross-entropy loss function is further incorporated to train the classification models, forcing the classifier to build smoother and more robust decision boundaries. The theoretical framework of LSG-SMOTE provides a novel perspective on over-sampling by bridging the gap between feature-space synthesis and label-space smoothing, effectively enhancing the generalization capability of classifiers on skewed data distributions.

title: Prototype Blending SMOTE++: Over-Sampling for Imbalanced Data Based on Semantic Fusion of Multi-Class Prototypes
abstract: Class imbalance remains a critical and challenging issue in the fields of machine learning and data mining. Traditional Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE) and its variants predominantly rely on linear interpolation between local nearest neighbors. However, when dealing with complex manifold structures, high-dimensional sparse spaces, or severe noise interference, such neighborhood-based interpolation methods are prone to overfitting or concept drift, failing to capture the true semantic characteristics of the minority class. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes a novel over-sampling framework named Prototype Blending SMOTE++ (PB-SMOTE++). Moving away from traditional point-to-point geometric interpolation, the proposed method integrates macro-level and micro-level semantics. By utilizing adaptive density clustering within the minority class, the framework extracts multiple representative "class prototypes." It then performs non-linear "semantic fusion" and dynamic perturbation across these multiple prototypes within an implicit semantic space, thereby generating new samples that possess both strong generalization capabilities and robust class representation. We provide a rigorous theoretical foundation, detailed algorithmic architecture, and comprehensive mathematical derivations for PB-SMOTE++, highlighting its unique advantages in preserving the intrinsic manifold structure and mitigating noise sensitivity when handling complex, imbalanced datasets.

title: Robustness of Intermediate-Task Training in Zero-Shot Transfer to Low-Resource Languages
abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. We investigate whether English intermediate-task training is still helpful on non-English target tasks. Using nine intermediate language-understanding tasks, we evaluate intermediate-task transfer in a zero-shot cross-lingual setting on the XTREME benchmark. We see large improvements from intermediate training on the BUCC and Tatoeba sentence retrieval tas Research goal: To what extent does intermediate-task training on English data improve robustness against typological distance when evaluating zero-shot transfer on low-resource languages within the XTREME benchmark? title: Study of Seismic Activity Between the Mainshock and the First Aftershock of the Kamchatka Earthquake on July 29, 2025
abstract: The high-amplitude seismic waves generated by the earthquakes with magnitudes similar to that of the July 29, 2025 Kamchatka event (MW 8.8) create the background noise that can potentially mask any post-seismic activity during the first few minutes following the mainshock. Detection of signals from potential aftershocks buried in the coherent noise can be enhanced using a matched filter detector based on waveform cross-correlation with high-quality waveform templates obtained from historical events in the same region. The array stations of the International Monitoring System (IMS) located at regional and teleseismic distances provide one of the most effective networks for detecting seismic events globally. However, the coherence between noise signals and the sought signals, as generated by very similar sources in the same area, makes less efficient the detection methods based on noise suppression by velocity filtering such as beamforming. For the event on July 29, 2025 near Kamchatka Peninsula, the noise reduction method based on adding stochastic noise to the actual data was tested. During the initial 10-minute period following the mainshock, several reliable event hypotheses were created. These hypotheses are similar to those reported by the International Data Centre (IDC) and are based on the data from the same IMS stations. The IDC and the International Seismological Centre had not reported any events during this time frame, despite extended automatic and interactive analyses.

title: Disentangling Pictorial Cue Understanding from Language Bias in VLMs via Depth Ordering Task
abstract: In this paper, we study depth perception of vision-language models (VLMs) to isolate the effects of pictorial depth cues and disentangle vision and language influences on model performance. To this end, we combine depth-ordering and odd-one-out psychophysical tasks: the VLMs are presented with images where one object is at different depth relative to other, otherwise identical, objects, and must determine whether the odd-one-out target is closer or farther to the observer. To create stimuli, we generate 2D views from simulated and real 3D scenes while controlling the presence of individual pictorial depth cues, enabling a fine-grained analysis of cue-level contributions. Language effects are examined by varying referring expression clarity. We also introduce a novel metric to quantify vision-vs-language sensitivities. Applying this methodology, we create the Odd-One-Out Depth (O3-D) dataset with 37K real and synthetic images and 147K image-question pairs. Evaluation of 12 open-source and commercial models on O3-D shows under-utilization of depth cues and depth-ordering accuracies between 47% and 56%, with no model above chance level. At the same time, our metric reveals strong linguistic bias in the answers. evidence.title: Disentangling Pictorial Cue Understanding from Language Bias in VLMs via Depth Ordering Task
evidence.abstract: In this paper, we study depth perception of vision-language models (VLMs) to isolate the effects of pictorial depth cues and disentangle vision and language influences on model performance. To this end, we combine depth-ordering and odd-one-out psychophysical tasks: the VLMs are presented with images where one object is at different depth relative to other, otherwise identical, objects, and must determine whether the odd-one-out target is closer or farther to the observer. To create stimuli, we generate 2D views from simulated and real 3D scenes while controlling the presence of individual pictorial depth cues, enabling a fine-grained analysis of cue-level contributions. title: LC-QAT: Data-Efficient 2-Bit QAT for LLMs via Linear-Constrained Vector Quantization
abstract: Quantization-aware training (QAT) is essential for extremely low-bit large language models (LLMs). Current QAT methods are mainly based on scalar quantization (SQ), which enables efficient optimization but suffers from severe performance degradation at 2-bit precision. On the other hand, vector quantization (VQ) provides substantially higher representational capacity, but its discrete codebook lookup prevents end-to-end training. We propose LC-QAT, a 2-bit weight-only VQ-QAT framework that represents quantized weights via a learned affine mapping over discrete vectors, which yields a high-quality PTQ initialization and enables fully differentiable end-to-end optimization without explicit codebook lookup in the training forward pass. This strong post-training initialization makes LC-QAT highly data-efficient. Experiments across diverse LLMs demonstrate that LC-QAT consistently outperforms state-of-the-art QAT methods while using only 0.1%--10% of the training data. Our results establish LC-QAT as a practical and scalable solution for extreme low-bit model deployment. Codes are publicly available at https://github.com/AI9Stars/UniSVQ.

title: The Third-Generation Cross-Institutional Encrypted Collaboration: A Review of MPC-TEE Fusion in Medical Privacy AI
abstract: With the increasingly stringent global data protection regulations and the growing demand for cross-institutional collaboration, traditional privacy computing technologies can hardly meet the requirements for efficient, secure and scalable collaboration. The third-generation cross-institutional encryption technology takes the fusion of Secure Multi-Party Computation (MPC) and Trusted Execution Environment (TEE) as the core, and better balances security and performance through the collaborative design of software and hardware. In the fields of healthcare, financial services, the Internet of Things and others, MPC-TEE fusion technology can realize efficient collaboration while ensuring data privacy, further promoting the industrialization of privacy AI. However, this technology still faces challenges such as side-channel attacks, insufficient standardization and high costs. This paper systematically reviews the latest research progress of MPC-TEE fusion technology, deeply analyzes its technical foundation, fusion principles and core architecture design, compares and analyzes the application performance and scenario adaptability of mainstream technical frameworks in the medical field, and discusses the security threats faced by the technology and multi-level defense mechanisms. It also looks forward to the development trends and research directions under the fusion of post-quantum cryptography, edge computing and other technologies, providing a reference for the large-scale implementation, optimization and upgrading of this technology in the field of medical privacy AI.

title: Why Fable 5 and Mythos Behave Differently: A Hypothesis of Innergent State Compression in Ultra-Large Sparse Language Models
abstract: This paper proposes a theoretical hypothesis for understanding a qualitative shift in inference behavior in ultra-large language models of the Fable/Mythos class, especially sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) systems at the multi-trillion-parameter scale. The central claim is that beyond a critical capacity threshold, inference ceases to rely primarily on explicit token-by-token retention in the key–value (KV) cache and instead increasingly leverages highly specialized parametric subnetworks that can serve as direct “hits” for semantically structured queries. We call this proposed regime Innergent State Compression (ISC).The paper has three goals. First, it formalizes the notion of dead-weight accu- mulation in long-context inference: a condition in which a growing KV cache stores many past tokens whose marginal utility for future generation becomes negligible while their memory cost remains linear. Second, it introduces the concept of in- nergence, defined as an internally reorganizing transition caused by external scale growth, in contrast to emergence, where simple internals generate rich external be- havior. Third, it uses this framework to explain why two models that may share a common sparse backbone—such as a public safety-constrained variant and a re- stricted less-constrained variant—can exhibit materially different outward behavior while preserving the same core competence.The paper does not claim a formal proof, privileged access to proprietary model internals, or experimental verification of the full mechanism. Rather, it offers a falsi- fiable conceptual model with explicit predictions: if ISC is real, then sufficiently large sparse models should show decreasing dependence on full-cache retention, improved robustness under aggressive cache eviction, lower routing entropy for familiar tasks, and superior long-context efficiency not fully explained by training quality alone. In this sense, ISC is presented not as established doctrine but as a research program for studying the next inference regime beyond conventional Transformer scaling.

abstract: A crucial distinction needs to be made here: "intelligence species" and "biological species" exist on entirely different levels.
